newsitem.title: USA: USWC gasoline shifts to May, prices up with NYMEX.
newsitem.headline: USWC gasoline shifts to May, prices up with NYMEX.

text.p: Prices for U.S. West Coast gasoline were pegged the same for April and May Monday, as traders shifted their focus to next month and tracked gains in energy futures.
Crude oil for May delivery made strong gains as NYMEX traders bought the contract to cover their shorts, a position which meant they initially though prices would fall.
Nearby crude rose 44 cents a barrel to $20.35 in late trade, while unleaded gasoline climbed 1.21 cents a gallon.
Traders scrambled before the May crude contract expired Tuesday.
"We're up on the screen," one player said.

April/May prices for CARB (California Air Resources Board) unleaded gasoline in Los Angeles were talked one cent higher than Friday at 72 to 73 cents, with some traders noting a year-on-year drop in West Coast stocks lent support.
San Francisco CARB cost the same Monday.
A swap of CARB for conventional gasoline was reported by a large refiner Monday. The deal involved an unknown quantity of CARB for conventional, which stood 5.5 cents a gallon cheaper.
Two cargoes of CARB were slated to arrive this week, but traders did not immediately know when they would come.
"Most of the barrels on board are sold," a trader said, added the market would not drop on the arriving barrels, he said.
L.A. low sulphur diesel dropped one cent a gallon to 60/61 cents, with traders saying a cargo of fuel was delivered
